# Source Catalog

The **Live access** table is generated by `python3 research/rdb.py probe && python3 research/rdb.py catalog`;
everything else is maintained by hand. "Expected" columns are plans, not observations.

Notes on the live results:

- The generated table shows the latest row per source; content-level re-test rows (2026-10-16T17:28Z) supersede the
  probe's bare HTTP status (e.g. Reddit (old) JSON "ok" was actually a login page).
- `proxy_denied` means the session's network policy blocked the host before any request reached the site.
  It says nothing about whether the site itself would allow us.
- The GitHub REST API answers 403 for a different reason: this session's GitHub access is limited to the
  configured repository. Adding `api.github.com` to the allowlist does not change that (see GitHub row below).

## Tool-level findings (re-tested 2026-10-16 ~17:28Z, after the network policy was widened)

Content-level checks (an HTTP 200 alone is not counted: each page was inspected for real content).

| Tool / route | Observed behaviour | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Shell HTTP (curl / Python) | Network policy no longer blocks research hosts. | `rdb.py snap` / `fetch` are the retrieval path. |
| Reddit direct (`www`/`old` `.json`) | **Reddit itself** blocks: `old.reddit.com` redirects to `/login/?reason=lor2`, `www` returns 403 (both user agents). | Not used. |
| Arctic Shift archive | Full post text + comment trees work. Search sometimes answers "Timeout. Maybe slow down a bit". | Reddit route. `rdb.py snap <reddit thread URL>` goes through it and backs off. Archive may lag or miss deleted posts. |
| Capterra / GetApp | Review pages load; review text is embedded as JSON in the page. | Main review-site route. `verify` now reads script-embedded text. |
| G2, Trustpilot, Product Hunt | 403 from the sites' bot protection. | Not used; Capterra/GetApp instead. |
| AccountingWEB | Cloudflare challenge page, no content. | Not used; Reddit accounting subs instead. |
| BiggerPockets, Shopify Community, Shopify App Store, WordPress.org | Real content returned. | Used. |
| HN Algolia, Stack Exchange API | Real content returned. | Used. |
| QuickBooks Community, Wayback | Connect, but slow (>20 s); probe timeout reports `error`. | Usable with a longer timeout. |
| WebSearch | Works; titles, URLs, model-written summary. | Leads only; never quoted. |
| WebFetch | Works now (returned BiggerPockets topic list). Output is a model summary. | Never quoted; pages are snapped instead. |
| Apify connector | Not re-tested; not needed. | Not used. |

## Sources by type

| Source | Used for | Access route (preferred → fallback) | Auth | Expected issues | Segments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reddit | Complaints, workarounds, "what do you use" threads | Public `.json` endpoints → Arctic Shift archive API → none | None initially | Reddit often blocks unauthenticated data-centre traffic; outcome unknown until probed | All |
| Hacker News | Developer pain, "Ask HN", "I'd pay for" comments | Algolia HN Search API | None | Low | Developers, agencies |
| G2 | Reviews of incumbent tools (likes/dislikes) | Direct page fetch | None | Strong bot protection likely; may stay unreachable | All B2B |
| Capterra / GetApp | Reviews with pros/cons, company size | Direct page fetch | None | Bot protection likely | All B2B |
| Product Hunt | Launched competitors, launch comments | Page fetch → GraphQL API (needs a free developer token) | Token for API | Pages are JS-heavy | Developers, agencies, e-commerce |
| GitHub | Feature requests / issues on OSS competitors | Attach specific public repos to the session (read) → WebSearch `site:github.com` leads | Session repo scope | REST search is limited to the configured repo | Developers |
| Stack Exchange | Repeated how-to questions = workaround evidence | Stack Exchange API (no key needed at low volume) | None | Low | Developers, bookkeeping (money.SE) |
| Shopify App Store | 1–3 star app reviews with dates | Direct page fetch | None | Low–medium | E-commerce |
| Shopify Community | Merchant forum threads | Direct page fetch | None | Medium | E-commerce |
| WordPress.org | Plugin reviews and support threads | Plugin API + page fetch | None | Low | E-commerce, agencies |
| QuickBooks / Xero community | Accounting-tool complaints and workarounds | Direct page fetch | None | Medium | Bookkeeping |
| AccountingWEB "Any Answers" | UK practitioner forum | Direct page fetch | None | Low | Bookkeeping |
| BiggerPockets forums | Landlord workflows and tools | Direct page fetch | None | Some pages login-gated | Landlords |
| Trustpilot | Consumer-facing complaints about SaaS vendors | Direct page fetch | None | Bot protection possible | All |
| Competitor websites | Pricing, positioning, feature lists | Direct page fetch, added per competitor | None | Each domain must be allowlisted | All |
| Wayback Machine | Historic pricing pages, removed posts | Direct fetch | None | Low | All |
| Job postings | Repeated manual workflows | WebSearch leads → public ATS pages (Greenhouse, Lever) | None | Indeed/LinkedIn block bots and forbid scraping; excluded | All |

Excluded on purpose: LinkedIn, Facebook groups, X, Quora (login walls or terms prohibit scraping).

## Reddit without credentials

1. Try public `.json` endpoints at ≤1 request / 2 s with a descriptive user agent.
2. If Reddit refuses them, use the Arctic Shift archive (third-party, free, may lag or have gaps).
3. Only if both fail **and** Reddit evidence is the deciding gap for a shortlisted segment, request a
   Reddit API "script" app (registered under the Reddit account; check Reddit's current Data API terms and
   any commercial-use conditions before creating it). No credentials are requested before that point.
